editorialHook: San Francisco is slipping into its coziest, most magical mode this week, with twinkling lights coming on all over the city just in time for Thanksgiving.

picks.d: Your Valkyries are CHAMPIONS and San Francisco is throwing them the party they deserve. Line up along the Embarcadero starting at 9am and cheer your heart out as the parade rolls from the Ferry Building toward Oracle Park. This is a once-in-a-generation moment for Bay Area basketball - do not miss it.

picks.t: Lightscape at SF Botanical Garden - Opening Night
picks.d: One million lights transform Golden Gate Park into a glowing winter wonderland tonight - and every night through January. Walk a one-mile trail through luminous art installations, optical illusions, and all-new color and sound experiences woven through the garden's ancient trees. Grab tickets fast because weekend slots sell out early.

picks.t: Great Dickens Christmas Fair - Opening Weekend
picks.w: Sat Nov 21 + Sun Nov 22 · All Day
picks.d: Victorian London takes over the Cow Palace this weekend as the 42nd Annual Great Dickens Christmas Fair swings open its doors. Hundreds of costumed characters roam 140,000 square feet of pubs, music halls, festive shops, and theatrical streets straight out of a Dickens novel. Active military get in free the first two weekends, and early bird tickets save you a few bucks.

picks.t: The Mountain Goats - Night Six: Closers
picks.d: John Darnielle and company wrap up their extraordinary six-night Fillmore residency tonight with 'Closers,' the grand finale of a week-long journey through their catalog. This is the kind of run that becomes a legend in SF concert history - intimate, emotional, and utterly one-of-a-kind. If you only catch one night of this residency, make it the last one.

picks.t: The Mountain Goats - Night Five: Cast of Thousands
picks.d: Night Five of the Mountain Goats' epic Fillmore residency digs into 'Cast of Thousands,' one of the band's most beloved eras. The Fillmore's intimate size makes every set here feel like a secret show just for you, and John Darnielle's storytelling between songs is as good as the music itself. Friday night at the Fillmore - does it get more SF than that?

picks.t: SF SPCA Holiday Windows at Macy's - Opens Today
picks.d: For 40 years running, the SF SPCA has filled Macy's Union Square windows with the most irresistible holiday display in the city - adorable, adoptable puppies and kittens doing their cutest thing for passersby on Powell Street. It is completely free, it is open Wednesday through Sunday through New Year's Eve, and yes, you are absolutely allowed to press your nose against the glass. Fair warning: you may leave with a new pet.

picks.t: Divine Offering: Celebrating the Legacy of Alice Coltrane
picks.d: Sita Michelle Coltrane leads a rare and reverential tribute to her mother, Alice Coltrane, one of jazz's most transcendent spiritual artists. Presented by GAMH and Psyched! Fest, this is exactly the kind of soul-nourishing, once-in-a-blue-moon event that makes San Francisco's music scene so special. Tickets run $39.50 to $45 and this one will sell out.

picks.t: SFMOMA - Sarah Sze: Forever is Composed of Nows - Opening
picks.d: Sarah Sze takes over SFMOMA's massive ground-floor atrium for her most ambitious commission yet - three paintings up to 27 feet tall colliding with video projection, sound, and light that spill up through multiple floors of the museum. It is free to experience on the first floor, which is a genuinely wild gift. This one is going to become the must-see installation of the season.

picks.t: Dear San Francisco: Home for the Holidays at Club Fugazi
picks.d: The critically adored circus-meets-theater experience at Club Fugazi gets a full holiday makeover for its festive seasonal run. World-class acrobats from the 7 Fingers collective perform aerial acts, Korean plank, Chinese pole, juggling, and hand-to-trap inside the intimate North Beach venue. It is the most charming date night in the city right now, full stop.

picks.t: The Nightmare Before Christmas with Live Orchestra
picks.d: Tim Burton's beloved dark fantasy gets the full Davies Symphony Hall treatment - the film plays on screen while a live orchestra performs Danny Elfman's iconic score in real time. This is an annual SF tradition that hits a little different when you are watching Jack and Sally while a world-class ensemble plays five feet away. Perfect mid-week Thanksgiving treat.

Exploratorium's beloved Glow exhibition kicks off its season with an adults-only After Dark opening night at Pier 15 - luminescent creatures, glowing T. rex skeletons, optical illusions, and bioluminescent wonders await. Weekend daytime Glow events also run Saturday and Sunday for all ages. It is science, it is art, and it is an absolute blast.

picks.t: SF Turkey Trot in Golden Gate Park
picks.d: Start Thanksgiving morning the right way with the 24th annual Turkey Trot through Golden Gate Park - choose from a 5-mile run, a 3-mile run, or a 100-meter dash for the little ones. It is festive, it is free-spirited, and burning those pre-feast calories with a few hundred happy strangers is genuinely one of the best feelings this city has to offer. Register online in advance.

picks.t: Indigenous Peoples Thanksgiving Sunrise Ceremony - Alcatraz
picks.d: Watch the sun rise over the Bay from Alcatraz Island at this powerful and moving annual gathering organized by the International Indian Treaty Council, commemorating the 1969-71 occupation of Alcatraz by the Indians of All Tribes. The boat ticket runs $12 for adults and the ceremony itself is free. It is a profound and unforgettable way to spend Thanksgiving morning.

ongoing.t: SFMOMA - RM x SFMOMA: Between You and Me
ongoing.d: Nearly 150 works from BTS member RM's personal collection alongside SFMOMA holdings - one of the largest presentations of Korean modern art in the US, through Feb 7.

ongoing.t: SFMOMA - Graciela Iturbide: Between Two Worlds
ongoing.d: Last week to catch this stunning black-and-white photo survey from the Mexico City master - closes Nov 29, do not sleep on it.

ongoing.t: de Young - Treasures of the Pharaohs
ongoing.d: US premiere of 130 artifacts from the Egyptian Museum in Cairo and the Luxor Museum - Bay Area residents get free admission every Saturday.

ongoing.t: de Young - Rooted in Place: California Native Art
ongoing.d: Gorgeous reimagining of the Indigenous America galleries exploring art, ceremony, and land through Dec 6.

ongoing.t: Asian Art Museum - Ha Chong-Hyun Retrospective
ongoing.d: Sixty years of innovative Korean abstraction on hemp cloth - a sensory journey through Jan 25.

ongoing.t: Asian Art Museum - Vishnu's Cosmic Ocean
ongoing.d: Southeast Asia's largest ancient bronze makes a once-in-a-lifetime US stop, through Jan 25.

ongoing.t: ACT - John Proctor Is the Villain
ongoing.d: West Coast premiere of Kimberly Belflower's sharp coming-of-age play, with post-show talks on Nov 24 and 25.

bars.name: Dalva
bars.d: Long-running Mission cocktail institution co-owned by Downtime's Eric Ochoa - neighborhood warmth with serious bartending chops.

bars.name: Bar Coto
bars.d: Daytime espresso becomes evening aperitivo at the Tusks' walk-in-only gem in Jackson Square.

bars.name: Bar Antoine Lounge
bars.d: Tucked above Le Parc Bistrobar at the Galleria Park Hotel - a civilized pre-theater or post-shopping cocktail spot.

bars.name: F8
bars.d: Interzone Darkwave Tuesdays every week - $5 after 10pm, 21+, and the city's best room for goth and EBM.

bars.name: 1015 Folsom
bars.d: The SoMa institution anchoring the club week - Westend Friday and Andy C on Wednesday, full multi-room experience.

bars.name: Public Works
bars.d: FJAAK and Hiroko Yamamura Friday, DEATHPACT Saturday - two of the best electronic bookings in town this week.

bars.name: Rickshaw Stop

High-stakes in-state NBA Cup clash with Sacramento.

sports.note: And of course - cheer the Valkyries at their Championship Parade on Thanksgiving morning along the Embarcadero!

games.detail: Parade from Ferry Building along the Embarcadero toward Oracle Park. Fan line-up begins at 9am.

sports.note: This is the one. Be there.

concerts.t: The Mountain Goats - Night Five: Cast of Thousands
concerts.d: Night Five of an extraordinary six-show Fillmore residency, each night themed around a different era of their catalog. John Darnielle's storytelling and emotional intensity make every night feel essential - this one digs into the beloved 'Cast of Thousands' chapter. See it tonight, then come back tomorrow for the finale.

concerts.t: The Mountain Goats - Night Six: Closers
concerts.d: The grand finale of one of the most ambitious residencies the Fillmore has hosted in years - 'Closers' wraps up six nights of deep catalog dives with the kind of emotional payoff only the Mountain Goats can deliver. This is a show people will be talking about for years. Get your ticket.

concerts.t: Divine Offering: Celebrating the Legacy of Alice Coltrane
concerts.d: Sita Michelle Coltrane and special guests honor the cosmic, spiritual genius of Alice Coltrane in a rare and reverent tribute presented by GAMH and Psyched! Fest. Alice Coltrane's music rewired what jazz could be - harp, organ, strings, and devotion all woven together into something transcendent. One of the most meaningful concerts of the year.

The Faroese singer-songwriter brings her hauntingly beautiful Nordic folk and cinematic soundscapes to August Hall for a night that feels like it belongs in a fjord under the northern lights. Eivör weaves ancient vocal traditions with modern production in a way that is utterly unlike anything else on the bill this week. A quiet stunner of a show.

concerts.t: Jayski and the Dawn featuring Jay Lane and Dave Ellis
concerts.d: A groove-heavy jazz night at the GAMH anchored by two of the Bay Area's most respected instrumentalists - Jay Lane's drumming alone is worth the ticket. If you want something warm and funky to ease into your Friday, this is your room. Doors at 7, show at 8.
concerts.venue: Great American Music Hall · Check gamh.com

concerts.d: The indie king who gave us Something Corporate and Jack's Mannequin brings his solo catalog to the intimate GAMH stage for a Saturday night that will hit you right in the feelings. His live shows are piano-forward, emotionally generous, and completely disarming - exactly the kind of night you want when the holidays are creeping in. Doors at 6.
concerts.venue: Great American Music Hall · Check gamh.com

concerts.t: Jonas Brothers - The Burning Up Tour All Over Again
concerts.d: The JoBros roll into Chase Center fresh off a Madison Square Garden sellout run, with Magnus Ferrell, Franklin Jonas, and All Time Low joining as special guests. If you have been a fan since the Disney Channel days or just want a giant, fun arena pop show the night before Thanksgiving, this is your move. It is going to be loud, joyful, and absolutely packed.

concerts.t: DEATHPACT: From Darkness, Comes Light: Eclipsed
concerts.d: Public Works transforms into a full-space immersive club experience with DEATHPACT headlining alongside Jiqui and DJ Dials for a limited-capacity night built to sell out. Dark, hypnotic, and absolutely the underground alternative to the arena show happening across town. Tickets run $15 to $30, 21+, and yes - this one will sell out.

The legendary Bay Area rapper is a true cult hero of SF hip-hop - his devoted hometown crowd turns every GAMH show into a celebration. If you are in town for Thanksgiving week and want to do something genuinely local and special, this is your night. Doors at 7.
concerts.venue: Great American Music Hall · Check gamh.com

concerts.d: The founder of Ram Records and one of drum and bass's most iconic figures ever headlines 1015 Folsom for a mid-week Thanksgiving eve banger. Andy C is the rare DJ who can make a room feel like it is levitating - if you are not making it home for the holiday until Thursday morning, stay out for this. Tickets $22 to $32, 21+, 9pm to 2am.

concertsOngoing.t: Brian Blade at SFJAZZ Miner Auditorium
concertsOngoing.d: One of jazz's most celebrated and spiritually sensitive drummers performs Sunday Nov 22 - check sfjazz.org for tickets.

concertsOngoing.t: SF Symphony Youth Orchestra at Davies
concertsOngoing.d: One of the country's most prestigious youth orchestras performs Sunday Nov 22 at 6pm - a beautiful pre-Thanksgiving concert.
British post-hardcore with intense emotional live sets Sunday Nov 22 - check augusthallsf.com.
Buzzed-about experimental metal act with Dry Socket and Pure Hex on Saturday Nov 21.
Kosovo-born genre-defying vocalist blending Balkan folk with pop and soul, Sunday Nov 22, $25-$28, all ages.

concertsOngoing.t: Endzeit x Non Series at TBA Downtown
concertsOngoing.d: Luigi Tozzi, Psyk, Neel, and more for a deep underground techno night Friday Nov 20 - follow @EndzeitSF for venue reveal.

singles.d: Hosted at a yoga studio on Union Street by The Tantra Institute, this is not your average speed dating night - chemistry games, conscious connection, and a claimed 94% connection rate make it one of the more intentional ways to meet someone in this city. Come with an open mind and comfortable clothes. Singles looking for something a little more meaningful than small talk will love this format.

Meet 8 to 12 local singles in one focused, fun night at The Jay Hotel - SpeedSanFrancisco runs tight, well-organized events with a clear age bracket so you are always meeting relevant people. Sunday evening is a surprisingly great time for this: low-key, early enough to be home at a reasonable hour, and the holiday-week energy adds a fun warmth to the room.

A relaxed social mixer format specifically for singles in their thirties - no pressure, no buzzers, just meeting people over drinks in a thoughtfully curated setting. The Comeunity Project events are known for attracting genuinely interesting humans who are tired of apps and ready to meet IRL. Thanksgiving week energy makes everyone a little more open and sociable.

singles.t: Gay Men Speed Dating - Fancy a Go?
singles.d: Part of the recurring 'Fancy a Go?' series, this welcoming and well-run speed dating night for gay men takes place Tuesday at The Jay Hotel - a fun mid-week Thanksgiving-week option that beats staying home and doom-scrolling. The structured format takes the awkwardness out of the introduction and leaves the fun parts in.

Fall Out Boy, My Chemical Romance, Paramore, and all the anthems of your formative years packed into the Rickshaw Stop's intimate dancefloor for one of the most social nights in the city. Emo Nite is legitimately one of the best ways to meet people in SF - shared nostalgia is the ultimate icebreaker and everyone in that room has the same emotional damage. In the best way.

Meet founders, investors, operators, and creators for an easy social run at Murphy Windmill in Golden Gate Park, followed by coffee and conversation. If you are new to SF or just want to expand your circle with interesting people before the holiday weekend kicks off, this is an unbeatable free option. They explicitly say they want you comfortable - no one is racing.

singlesOngoing.t: November Project SF - Free Weekly Workouts
singlesOngoing.d: Free, radically inclusive community workouts multiple mornings a week across SF - no signup, no pace requirement, just show up and make friends.

singlesOngoing.t: Marina Run Club - Tues and Thurs
singlesOngoing.d: SF's biggest social run club meets Tuesday at 7am and Thursday at 7am and 5:30pm at Marina Green and Duboce Park - free to join.
Tuesday nights in Golden Gate Park, Thursday nights at Kezar for speedwork, Saturday mornings around the city - all paces welcome.

date.title: Lights, Pups, and Pie
date.tagline: A Thanksgiving-week date that costs nothing but time

steps.title: SF SPCA Holiday Windows at Macy's
steps.detail: Start at Union Square and press your faces against the windows together watching adoptable puppies and kittens do their thing. Free, festive, and an instant mood booster.

steps.title: Walk to Golden Gate Park
steps.detail: Grab a coffee to go from any of the great spots on Haight Street and walk into the park together - this week it has a little extra magic with Lightscape setting up.

steps.title: de Young - Rooted in Place
steps.detail: Free with general admission, this beautiful Indigenous California art exhibition is quietly one of the best things in the park right now - thoughtful conversation guaranteed.

steps.title: Lightscape at SF Botanical Garden
steps.detail: Okay, this one requires a ticket ($32 adults) - but starting at 5pm the garden transforms into one million lights and it is absolutely worth every penny for a first date or a tenth.

date.title: Art, Acrobats, and Italian
date.tagline: Culture, wonder, and a plate of pasta

steps.title: Lauren Elkin at City Lights - Free
steps.detail: Start the morning with the free City Lights author event on Saturday the 21st - literary conversation is a great date energy and City Lights is one of SF's most romantic spots.

steps.title: Lunch at Lucania - Ferry Building
steps.detail: The brand-new Southern Italian spot just opened Nov 19 at the Ferry Building - grab a table on their renovated patio and order everything. Opening week energy is contagious.

steps.title: SFMOMA - Sarah Sze Opening + RM Collection
steps.detail: Sarah Sze's new monumental installation opens this Saturday - it is free on the first floor, then spring for admission to also see the RM x SFMOMA Korean art exhibition upstairs.

steps.title: Dear SF: Home for the Holidays at Club Fugazi
steps.detail: End the night with the most charming show in the city - world-class acrobats and heartfelt circus storytelling in an intimate North Beach venue. Tickets from around $79-$87.

date.title: Fillmore Friday
date.tagline: An iconic SF night from start to finish

steps.title: Dinner at Julius' Castle
steps.detail: The legendary hilltop restaurant just reopened after 18 years - panoramic Bay views, steak tartare, lamb chops, and pure old-school SF glamour. Book ahead.

steps.title: Mountain Goats Night Five at The Fillmore
steps.detail: Walk (or ride) to the Fillmore for Night Five of this historic six-show residency. John Darnielle on stage at 8pm in one of SF's most storied rooms - this is the date story you will tell forever.

steps.title: Nightcap at Bar Coto
steps.detail: Wind down with a late aperitivo at the Tusks' walk-in-only gem in Jackson Square - no reservations needed, just two people glowing from a perfect Friday in San Francisco.

solo.title: Thanksgiving Morning, Done Right
solo.tagline: Start the holiday with something that actually means something

steps.title: Indigenous Peoples Sunrise Ceremony - Alcatraz
steps.detail: Take the early boat ($12) to Alcatraz and join the International Indian Treaty Council's annual gathering as the sun rises over the Bay. Powerful, moving, and unlike anything else in the city.

steps.title: SF Turkey Trot - Golden Gate Park
steps.detail: Back on the mainland in time for the 24th annual Turkey Trot - 5 miles, 3 miles, or just cheer from the sidelines. The park at Thanksgiving morning is genuinely magical.

steps.title: Line up for the Valkyries Parade
steps.detail: Head to the Embarcadero early - fans can line up from 9am for the noon parade. Find your spot, get a coffee, and soak in one of the great civic celebrations of the year. Free.

steps.title: de Young - Treasures of the Pharaohs
steps.detail: Bay Area residents get in free every Saturday - but on Sunday treat yourself and linger over 130 extraordinary Egyptian artifacts from the Cairo and Luxor museums. No rush.

steps.title: Walk Lightscape Early Setup or Golden Gate Park
steps.detail: Spend the afternoon in the park, grab a bench by the Botanical Garden, and just breathe. The city is quieter on Sunday afternoons and Golden Gate Park in late November is stunning.

steps.title: Qendresa at Rickshaw Stop - All Ages
steps.detail: End the week with something genuinely surprising - Qendresa's Balkan folk-meets-soul vocals are like nothing else on a Sunday night in SF. Tickets $25-$28, all ages, doors at 7.

steps.title: Divine Offering: Alice Coltrane Tribute at GAMH
steps.detail: If you can only pick one, make it this - Sita Michelle Coltrane honoring her mother's spiritual jazz legacy is the most meaningful 90 minutes you can spend this week. $39.50-$45.

solo.title: The Art and Sound Tour
solo.tagline: Fill up your senses before Thanksgiving

steps.title: SFMOMA - Full Visit
steps.detail: Start with the free Sarah Sze installation on the ground floor, then pay for admission and dive into RM x SFMOMA. Budget two to three hours - this is a serious museum visit day.

steps.title: Lunch at Lucania - Ferry Building
steps.detail: Walk over to the brand-new Southern Italian opening at the Ferry Building and eat outside on their piazza-inspired patio. Opening-week menus always have extra energy.

steps.title: Exploratorium After Dark: Glow Opening
steps.detail: The Glow daytime weekend events run Saturday and Sunday 11am-4pm - luminescent creatures, light art, and bioluminescent wonders at Pier 15. Perfectly timed after lunch.

steps.title: Mountain Goats Night Six: Closers at The Fillmore
steps.detail: Cap the day with the grand finale of one of SF's most ambitious concert residencies. Treat yourself to a poster from the lobby. This is what Saturdays in this city are for.

steps.title: SF SPCA Holiday Windows at Macy's
steps.detail: Start the birthday with puppies and kittens at Macy's Union Square - completely free and immediately joyful. The birthday person gets bragging rights for the best morning activity.

steps.title: de Young - Free Saturday Admission for Bay Area Residents
steps.detail: Walk through Treasures of the Pharaohs or Rooted in Place for free on Saturday - a world-class museum birthday without spending a dime on admission.

steps.title: Lightscape Opening at SF Botanical Garden
steps.detail: Lightscape opens Friday Nov 20 and runs nightly from 5pm - split the ticket cost among the group ($32/adult) and walk through one million lights together on the birthday evening.

birthday.title: EMO NITE Birthday Bash
birthday.tagline: The only birthday theme that matters

steps.title: Pre-game dinner at Bar Coto - Jackson Square
steps.detail: Gather the crew at the Tusks' walk-in Italian cafe for aperitivo, wine, and housemade bread sandwiches before the main event. No reservations needed - perfect for a group.

steps.title: EMO NITE at Rickshaw Stop
steps.detail: Throw the birthday person into a room full of Fall Out Boy and My Chemical Romance anthems - the Rickshaw Stop floor is small enough that the whole group stays together and dances all night.

steps.title: Late drinks at Dalva
steps.detail: After EMO NITE winds down, migrate to the Mission's beloved Dalva for a proper late-night cocktail round. The birthday person picks the drink, everyone else toasts them.

birthday.title: Julius' Castle Birthday Comeback
birthday.tagline: Celebrate at the room that just came back from the dead

steps.title: Lightscape at SF Botanical Garden - Golden Hour Entry
steps.detail: Start early with the 5pm Lightscape entry - walking through a million lights in the botanical garden as a group sets the perfect tone for a birthday night.

steps.title: Dinner at Julius' Castle - North Beach
steps.detail: Book the whole table at the legendary hilltop restaurant just reopened after 18 years. Panoramic Bay views, old-school American menu, and the story of the comeback is itself the dinner conversation.

steps.title: Mountain Goats Finale or DEATHPACT
steps.detail: Split the group by vibe: emotional indie rock royalty at the Fillmore (Mountain Goats Night Six) or immersive underground techno at Public Works (DEATHPACT). Both are selling out - book ahead.

friends.title: Friendsgiving Warm-Up
friends.tagline: Turkey Trot, parade, and no money spent

steps.title: SF Turkey Trot - Golden Gate Park
steps.detail: Get the whole crew out for the Turkey Trot on Thanksgiving morning - 5 miles, 3 miles, or kids dash. Communal suffering before communal eating is a time-honored tradition.

steps.title: SF SPCA Holiday Windows at Macy's - Walk Over
steps.detail: Post-run, grab coffee and walk to Macy's Union Square to see the puppies and kittens. Free, festive, and everyone's heart grows three sizes.

steps.title: Line Up for Valkyries Championship Parade
steps.detail: Head to the Embarcadero, find the best spot, and cheer your lungs out for the Golden State Valkyries. Free, historic, and the ultimate Thanksgiving morning flex.

friends.title: Great Dickens Christmas Fair Crew Day
friends.tagline: Victorian chaos with your best people

steps.title: Great Dickens Christmas Fair - Cow Palace
steps.detail: Get to the Cow Palace for opening weekend of the 42nd Annual Dickens Fair - 140,000 square feet of Victorian London, pubs, music halls, and costumed characters. Budget 3-4 hours minimum.

steps.title: Post-Fair drinks at a SoMa bar
steps.detail: Decompress from Victorian London with a round at 1015 Folsom's bar or Public Works pre-show - decompress, laugh about your favorite Dickens character encounters, and plan the evening.

steps.title: Mountain Goats Night Five or Six at The Fillmore
steps.detail: End the day with a legendary show - the Mountain Goats Fillmore residency is the perfect Friday or Saturday night with a group of music lovers. Buy tickets in advance.

friends.title: The Thanksgiving Week Blowout
friends.tagline: Acrobats, jazz, and a 27-foot painting walk into a bar

steps.title: SFMOMA - Sarah Sze Opening + RM Collection
steps.detail: Start with the free Sze installation then pay for the full museum - the RM x SFMOMA Korean art collection is extraordinary and spending a few hours here together before a big night sets the right tone.

steps.title: Dinner at Fat Cat and The Mantis - Bernal Heights
steps.detail: 2026's most fun dinner spot per The Infatuation - natural wine, tagliatelle with mushroom nuoc cham, and Bernal Heights neighborhood energy. Book ahead for a group.

steps.title: Dear SF: Home for the Holidays at Club Fugazi
steps.detail: Walk or Lyft to North Beach for the holiday circus show - world-class acrobats in an intimate venue is genuinely the best group activity in the city this week. Everyone leaves grinning.

parents.title: Holiday Magic on Zero Budget
parents.tagline: Show the parents the SF that locals actually love

steps.title: SF SPCA Holiday Windows at Macy's - Union Square
steps.detail: Start downtown at the Macy's windows - 40 years of adorable adoptable animals is an icebreaker for any family visit and the Union Square holiday atmosphere is properly festive.

steps.title: Walk the Ferry Building + Lunch at Lucania
steps.detail: Walk the Embarcadero to the Ferry Building and grab lunch at the brand-new Lucania - Southern Italian all-day menu on the renovated patio with Bay views. Opening week makes it a fun story to share.

steps.title: de Young Museum - Free Saturday for Bay Area Residents
steps.detail: Free general admission on Saturdays for Bay Area residents - take your parents through Treasures of the Pharaohs and let them marvel at 3,000 years of Egyptian history.

parents.title: Tim Burton and Italian Wine
parents.tagline: A Thanksgiving week date night for the whole family

steps.title: Dinner at Bar Coto - Jackson Square
steps.detail: Pre-show dinner at the Tusks' all-day Italian cafe - no reservations, great wine, housemade bread, and the kind of relaxed neighborhood warmth that works perfectly with out-of-town guests.

steps.title: Walk Through Jackson Square
steps.detail: Jackson Square is one of SF's most beautiful and underrated neighborhoods - take a slow stroll through the historic blocks before heading to Davies Symphony Hall.

steps.title: Nightmare Before Christmas with Live Orchestra at Davies
steps.detail: The holiday tradition that works for literally every generation - Tim Burton's film with a live orchestra playing Elfman's score at Davies Symphony Hall on Tuesday Nov 24. Book tickets early.

parents.title: The Grand SF Thanksgiving Tour
parents.tagline: Show them why you live here

steps.title: Asian Art Museum - Vishnu's Cosmic Ocean
steps.detail: Start with the once-in-a-lifetime ancient bronze from Southeast Asia at the Asian Art Museum - this kind of object stops you in your tracks and sparks real conversation.

steps.title: Lunch at Julius' Castle - North Beach
steps.detail: Take your parents to the legendary hilltop restaurant that just reopened after 18 years - panoramic Bay views, steak tartare, and crab cakes. The comeback story alone makes for great table conversation.

steps.title: Lightscape at SF Botanical Garden
steps.detail: The most beautiful thing in the city this week - walk through a million lights in Golden Gate Park together as the sun goes down. Timed entry from 5pm, tickets from $32 adults.

steps.title: Dear SF: Home for the Holidays at Club Fugazi
steps.detail: Cap the visit with the holiday circus show in North Beach - intimate, funny, breathtaking, and entirely family-friendly. World-class acrobats in a small room is universally crowd-pleasing.
